Russia.md.assessment: Russia is likely to maintain military pressure on Ukraine while using selective diplomatic contacts to test limited arrangements and manage relations with European governments. The first Russia–Germany foreign-minister talks since 2022 and discussion of Black Sea navigation create channels for narrow functional agreements, but a broad ceasefire remains unlikely during this period.
likelyDevelopments: Russian drone and missile operations against Ukraine will continue, with jet-powered drones placing additional pressure on Ukrainian air defences.
European governments will strengthen their response to Russian sabotage, cyber activity and military movements around NATO airspace.

Diplomatic activity will probably continue through selective bilateral contacts and discussions about maritime security or energy infrastructure, but a comprehensive settlement remains unlikely during the forecast period.
The Kremlin will use the parliamentary-election result to reinforce the appearance of domestic support and institutional stability.

upcomingEvents.description: The UN General Assembly's general debate is scheduled to conclude, providing a near-term venue for diplomacy surrounding Ukraine.
EU defence ministers are scheduled to meet, with military support for Ukraine and regional defence readiness remaining relevant agenda areas.
EU restrictive measures addressing Russian hybrid activity are currently scheduled to expire, creating a decision point over renewal or replacement.
The European Council is scheduled to meet on 15–16 October and has said it will return to Ukraine and European defence readiness in October.

changeSignals: Russian acceptance of talks on a Black Sea or energy-infrastructure truce
A substantial reduction or increase in long-range attacks on Ukrainian cities
New EU sanctions or military-support commitments
Confirmed escalation involving Russian and NATO aircraft or infrastructure
Evidence that post-election domestic pressure is affecting Kremlin policy

Iran.md.assessment: Iran is likely to keep advocating a diplomatic, phased easing of pressure around the Strait of Hormuz while signalling readiness for renewed US attacks and refusing to fold its nuclear programme into the initial bargain. Trump's rejection of Tehran's current proposal makes an immediate shipping arrangement less likely, but further mediated offers remain plausible because both sides retain strong incentives to limit the conflict's economic costs.
likelyDevelopments: Tehran will continue to link freer passage through the Strait of Hormuz to relief from the US naval blockade and other economic pressure.
Iran will resist nuclear concessions in the near-term shipping negotiations, leaving the nuclear dispute on a separate and slower track.
The United States will press China and regional partners to use their economic and diplomatic leverage over Tehran.

Iran is likely to revise or re-present phased proposals through mediators while maintaining military readiness, but an immediate durable agreement is unlikely after Washington rejected the current offer.

upcomingEvents.description: The UN General Assembly's general debate is scheduled to conclude, closing the principal near-term venue for high-level diplomacy involving Iran and the United States.
The European Council is scheduled to meet on 15–16 October, providing a potential coordination point for European policy on Middle East security and shipping disruption.

changeSignals: A verified agreement on sequencing the reopening of the Strait and easing US pressure
Any Iranian willingness to include nuclear limits in negotiations
Changes in Chinese economic or diplomatic support for Tehran
A sustained increase or decrease in attacks affecting Gulf shipping
New sanctions, blockades or direct military action

Strait-of-Hormuz.md.assessment: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is likely to remain constrained after the United States rejected Iran's current reopening proposal. A revised phased arrangement could still restore some traffic, but Iran's refusal to make nuclear concessions and the continued US blockade of Iranian ports leave a high risk of prolonged or renewed disruption.
likelyDevelopments: Negotiators and mediators will probably explore revised staged steps that exchange greater freedom of navigation for relief from US pressure on Iranian ports.
Commercial shipping and energy markets will remain sensitive to military incidents and conflicting statements from Washington and Tehran.
Regional states will seek additional security coordination while avoiding actions that could expand the conflict.
Any initial accord is more likely to be narrow and operational than a comprehensive political settlement.

upcomingEvents.description: The UN General Assembly's general debate is scheduled to end, creating a natural checkpoint for diplomacy conducted around the New York meetings.
The European Council meets on 15–16 October, when the economic and security consequences of disrupted Gulf shipping may require further coordination.

changeSignals: Verified restoration of regular commercial transit
US relief from the naval blockade or sanctions affecting Iranian ports
A new Iranian transit-fee or inspection regime
Attacks on tankers, ports or naval forces
